Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the moment of mission accomplishment
Refined_Definition: Mission accomplishment denotes the transition at which an executing force realises the objective or end state assigned by its higher echelon, completing the commander's intent as set out in the operation order. At this granularity the event is a single evaluative transition: prior to accomplishment the mission status is open; after accomplishment the force's responsibility for the operation concludes [ADP 3-0; FM 6-0].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the act of taking into custody
Refined_Definition: Apprehension is the single act by which a person authorised under Article 7 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice takes another into custody, effected by notifying the subject of the intention to apprehend and of the offence charged [Manual for Courts-Martial, R.C.M. 302]. At this granularity the act is a transition from at-liberty to in-custody status; the continuing condition that follows is treated under Imprisonment.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a single lethal act against a single subject
Refined_Definition: At this resolution, killing is the act that transitions a person from alive to deceased. Its lawfulness in armed conflict is governed by the principles of distinction and proportionality and by the prohibition on attacking persons hors de combat and civilians not directly participating in hostilities [Geneva Conventions, Common Article 3; AP I, Art. 51; FM 6-27]. Multi-victim and campaign-level uses of the term are anti-atomic and fall outside this granularity.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the declarative act of laying down arms
Refined_Definition: Surrender is the single act by which a combatant or formation ceases resistance and submits to the authority of the adversary, conferring prisoner-of-war status on members of regular armed forces and other combatants who lay down their arms [GC III, Art. 4]. The continuing condition of detention that follows is treated under Imprisonment.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the discharge of a weapon
Refined_Definition: At this resolution the event is the single discharge act, governed by the standing rules of engagement [CJCSI 3121.01]. Discharge may be for engagement of an identified target, suppression, warning, or signalling; engagement firing requires positive identification of the target as a lawful military objective [FM 3-90; FM 6-27]. Sustained fires and fire missions, being phased and directed by a fire-support plan, are anti-atomic and fall outside this granularity.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the issuance of a finding
Refined_Definition: At this resolution the event is the single act by which the responsible authority records a compliance determination against prescribed standards for personnel, equipment, training, or operations [AR 1-201]. The preparatory examination activities that precede the finding are subordinated to the issuance act at this granularity; the broader command oversight process is treated separately under the commander's assessment cycle [FM 6-0].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical Transition Events (anti-cumulative, atomic, homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the granting or imposition act
Refined_Definition: At this resolution the event is the single authoritative act that confers an award or imposes a sanction. Awards are granted under the relevant service regulations [AR 600-8-22]; non-judicial punishment is imposed under Article 15 and judicial punishment under Articles 16 to 76 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice [MCM]. Deliberative proceedings that precede the act are excluded from this granularity.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the engagement-acquisition sequence preceding discharge
Refined_Definition: Aiming is the directed alignment of a weapon system on a designated target prior to engagement. At this granularity the event decomposes into distinguishable sub-phases (target detection, sight picture, refinement, hold) that are not themselves instances of aiming, justifying the anti-atomic and anti-homeomeric profile [ATP 3-21.8; DoD Dictionary].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: an offensive task at brigade level and below
Refined_Definition: An attack is a directed offensive task that destroys or defeats enemy forces, seizes and secures terrain, or both. At this granularity the operation comprises preparation, execution, and consolidation phases, each with internal structure not itself constituting an attack [FM 3-90]. Hasty and deliberate variants differ in planning time but share the phased structure.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a defensive operation against an identified enemy attack
Refined_Definition: A defensive operation is a directed operation conducted to defeat an enemy attack, gain time, economise force, and develop conditions favourable for offensive or stability operations [ADP 3-0; FM 3-90]. At this granularity the operation comprises preparation of positions, security operations forward of the main defence, and the integrated employment of fires and obstacles during the engagement, each phase being structurally distinct from the others.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a deliberate prosecution of encirclement against a fixed position
Refined_Definition: Besieging is the directed conduct of an encirclement intended to compel surrender of a fortified position or urban area through denial of resupply, reinforcement, and escape. At this granularity the operation comprises preparation, isolation, and reduction phases, each of which is not itself a siege [FM 3-90; JP 3-06].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the operational sequence by which effective control over territory is acquired
Refined_Definition: Conquering is the directed acquisition by a belligerent of effective control over identified territory through military force. At this granularity the event comprises seizure and consolidation of the objectives that constitute the territory, after which the occupying power assumes duties under GC IV and Section III of the Hague Regulations of 1907. Sub-phases (seizure, consolidation, transition to occupation administration) are structurally distinct.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a sequence of tactical actions sharing a common purpose
Refined_Definition: A military operation is a directed sequence of tactical actions with a common purpose or unifying theme [DoD Dictionary]. At this granularity the operation comprises planning, preparation, execution, and assessment activities [FM 6-0]. Categorisation by level (strategic, operational, tactical) and by nature (offensive, defensive, stability, defence support of civil authorities) does not alter the phased structure on which the meta-property profile is based [ADP 3-0].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a single patrol task under a higher echelon's order
Refined_Definition: Patrolling is the directed movement of a detachment through a designated area or along a designated route for a specified purpose such as reconnaissance, surveillance, area security, or combat [DoD Dictionary; ATP 3-21.8]. At this granularity the task comprises briefing, movement, action at objective, and return phases, none of which is itself a patrol.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: an investigation of a single alleged offence
Refined_Definition: A military criminal investigation is the directed examination of an alleged offence against the Uniform Code of Military Justice, conducted by trained investigators or by service criminal investigation organisations [AR 195-2; ATP 3-39.12]. At this granularity the investigation comprises preliminary inquiry, evidence collection, suspect interview, and submission of a final report, each phase structurally distinct.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a planned recovery of identified isolated personnel
Refined_Definition: Rescuing, in personnel recovery, is the directed and planned recovery of personnel from the territory or custody of an adversary, executed by combat search and rescue, special operations, or conventional forces [JP 3-50]. At this granularity the operation comprises insertion, recovery action, extraction, and reintegration, each phase distinct from the others.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a single evacuation task with a defined reception point
Refined_Definition: Evacuation is the directed removal of personnel, equipment, or materiel from a location to a place of safety or to a designated reception point [DoD Dictionary]. At this granularity the task comprises preparation, movement, and reception phases; doctrinal categories (CASEVAC, MEDEVAC, NEO) share this phased structure [JP 3-68; JP 4-02].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a single escape attempt by an interned combatant
Refined_Definition: Escaping is the directed act by which an interned combatant departs from the place of internment with the intention of rejoining their own forces. At this granularity the attempt comprises planning, breakout, evasion, and recovery phases; only on successful return to friendly forces does prisoner-of-war status terminate [GC III, Arts. 91-94; FM 6-27].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the directed conduct of internment as a continuing operation
Refined_Definition: Imprisonment is the directed internment of captured combatants or other persons taken into custody by a party to a conflict, beginning at capture and terminating at repatriation or release [GC III, Arts. 17-20; FM 6-27]. At this granularity the conduct comprises reception, sustained custody, and release phases, each governed by distinct doctrinal and legal requirements.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a single disclosure act by a person with authorised access
Refined_Definition: Unauthorised disclosure is the directed communication, by a person with authorised access, of information formally designated as protected against unauthorised disclosure, to persons not authorised to receive it [DoDM 5200.01; UCMJ Art. 134]. At this granularity the act comprises preparation, communication, and consequence-management phases when treated as a deliberate disclosure operation; in its instantaneous sense the act would fall under Group A.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the production and transmission of a single doctrinal report
Refined_Definition: Reporting is the directed transmission of information to a higher headquarters, subordinate unit, or supporting agency in a structured format [FM 6-0]. At this granularity the event comprises information collection, drafting in the prescribed format (SITREP, SPOTREP, OPREP), and transmission, each phase distinct [AR 25-50].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: the deliberate issuance of a formal communication by an authorised representative
Refined_Definition: A statement is the directed communication of information, intention, or position by an authorised representative of a military command. At this granularity the event comprises preparation, authorisation, and issuance phases. Sworn statements taken in military justice proceedings are governed by UCMJ Art. 31 [MCM, R.C.M. 305]; public statements are governed by service public-affairs doctrine [JP 3-61].

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a directed campaign or operation employing terrorist methods
Refined_Definition: Terrorism is the directed and unlawful use of violence or threat of violence, motivated by religious, political, or other ideological beliefs, to instil fear and coerce governments or societies in pursuit of political goals [DoD Dictionary; JP 3-07.2]. At this granularity the conduct comprises planning, preparation, execution, and exploitation phases. The definition applies whether the actor is a state, a state-sponsored proxy, or a non-state organisation.

Profile_Group_Description: Tactical and Operational Conduct -- Phased Operations (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, agentive)
Granularity: a directed application of physical force in armed conflict
Refined_Definition: Violence is the directed application of physical force against persons or property in armed conflict. Lawful violence against military objectives is governed by the principles of distinction, proportionality, and military necessity [AP I, Art. 48; FM 6-27]; violence against those not actively participating in hostilities is prohibited at all times and in all places [GC Common Article 3]. At this granularity the event comprises preparation, execution, and effect-assessment phases when treated as a directed application of force.

Profile_Group_Description: Non-Agentive Phenomena (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, non-agentive)
Granularity: a tactical conflict between opposing manoeuvre forces
Refined_Definition: An engagement is a tactical conflict between opposing manoeuvre forces, usually conducted at brigade level and below and normally lasting from minutes to a day [FM 3-90]. At this granularity the event has distinguishable contact, intensification, and disengagement phases and may result either from one side's deliberate offensive movement or from the meeting of forces during movement to contact. Because the engagement is constituted by the interaction of two opposing forces rather than the directed action of a single agent, the event is treated as non-agentive at the type level.

Profile_Group_Description: Non-Agentive Phenomena (anti-cumulative, anti-atomic, anti-homeomeric, non-agentive)
Granularity: the occurrence of physical injury to a person in armed conflict
Refined_Definition: Bodily harm is the occurrence of physical injury to a person during armed conflict, irrespective of whether it results from a directed engagement or from collateral effect. At this granularity the event has distinguishable causation, manifestation, and medical-response phases. Because instances of the type span both intentionally inflicted and incidental injuries, agentivity is not uniformly ascribable across all instances and the type is non-agentive at the type level [GC Common Article 3; FM 6-27].

Profile_Group_Description: Continuous Conditions and Status Predicates (cumulative, anti-atomic, homeomeric, non-agentive)
Granularity: a sustained condition of carrying arms in the conduct of military operations
Refined_Definition: Bearing arms is the sustained condition of carrying weapons openly in the conduct of military operations. At this granularity the condition holds uniformly across any sub-interval during which the criteria are satisfied: any portion of the interval is itself an interval of bearing arms, and contiguous intervals fuse into a longer interval of the same type. Lawful combatant status under GC III, Art. 4(A) and Art. 1 of the Hague Regulations of 1907 requires that arms be carried openly during operations, that the person bearing them be commanded by a responsible superior, and that a fixed distinctive sign be worn recognisable at a distance.
